articles.title: Don Bradman Cricket Jr Announced for PC and Consoles
articles.summary: With Cricket 26 developer Big Ant Studios holding somewhat of a monopoly on the cricket videogame genre for more than a decade, fans of the world's second most popular sport have been crying out for some competition within the genre.
body: In comparison, Don Bradman Cricket Jr is arriving eight years late and minus any official team or player licenses, beyond the inclusion of Australia's greatest ever batsman himself as an unlockable character. By completing a specific in-game challenge, players will apparently be able to drop the Don directly into the otherwise entirely generic Australian team, as well as gain access to a bonus minigame that recreates his famous knocking-a-golf-ball-into-a-water-tank-using-a-stump-fo-a-bat training exercise.

Elsewhere, Don Bradman Cricket Jr seems to be offering a fairly basic feature set, with unlicensed tournaments to play and a challenge mode to test your skills with, alongside split-screen support for two players. Not much is known about the actual gameplay, but the developers are promising that the experience of batting will ensure that "no two shots are ever truly the same." This despite the announcement trailer above seeming to show multiple versions of the same pull through mid-wicket.

articles.title: Jesse Eisenberg Says He 'Couldn't Get Movie Studio Parts' After Winning His Batman v. Superman Razzie
articles.summary: Jesse Eisenberg says he "couldn't get into studio movie parts" because he won a Worst Supporting Actor Razzie for playing Lex Luthor in Batman v. Superman. The Social Network star elaborated on what has become one of his most divisive roles when speaking at the BFI London Film Festival (via Variety…
body: "Listen, a lot of it just came from fear," he said when describing his shift away from studio roles. "I couldn’t get into movie studio parts anymore because I had won a Raspberry Award from [being in the] Batman movie … and I saw the trajectory."

Although the polarizing Batman v. Superman: Dawn of Justice does have its fair share of fans, Eisenberg's more eccentric performance as the Superman villain has remained one of its most controversial elements in the decade since its premiere. His acting was so…memorable that he walked away from the part with a Razzie for Worst Supporting Actor.

Winning at the Golden Raspberry Awards, which recognize the worst components in movies each year, isn't usually treated as an honor. No one wants to be told they are the "worst" at anything, and having that Razzie label attached to your name can sometimes even secure a person's place in the hall of filmmaking infamy.

articles.title: Resident Evil Director Is Already Thinking Sequels
articles.summary: Weapons director Zach Cregger took a very different approach with his new adaptation of Resident Evil. Rather than adapting the characters and narrative of Capcom's survival-horror game franchise, Cregger is instead translating what it feels like to exist in one of Resident Evil 's worst-case…
body: That may not sound like your typical franchise starter, but a sequel to Resident Evil is already looking likely.

Perhaps the most important indicator that Resident Evil will spawn a sequel is the movie's early box office performance. According to a report from Deadline, September's Resident Evil is already tracking toward a record-setting opening weekend for the franchise — somewhere between $35 million and $50 million domestically. Sony Pictures must be happy about that, considering the previous movie in the franchise, 2021's Resident Evil: Welcome to Raccoon City, finished its theatrical run with a $41.9 million worldwide haul.

Cregger himself might be on board for a sequel. He tells Polygon that he was thinking his Resident Evil journey would be a "one and done" flirtation with Capcom's IP. But after completing the film, he says he has more ideas for the franchise.
In an interview with Cregger, Polygon editor-in-chief Matt Patches asked the director if he was hoping to kickstart the franchise for a possible new trilogy.

articles.title: Taika Waititi Says His Star Wars Movie Is 'on Ice'
articles.summary: Director Taika Waititi has confirmed his long-in-development Star Wars movie is officially "on ice." The Thor: Ragnarok and Jojo Rabbit filmmaker provided Inverse with the update when speaking to the outlet during a press junket for his new film, Klara and the Sun.
body: "I hate to break this to you, but we're going to actually put it on ice and we're working on a different thing together," he said.

Brutal. Rumors that Disney and Lucasfilm had approached the What We Do in the Shadows filmmaker to helm a Star Wars project go as far back as January 2020. That's just a few years after he took off as the mastermind behind one of the most beloved Marvel Cinematic Universe movies to date, with an official announcement confirming he was attached to a movie arriving just a few months later.

It was mostly good news at first. In 2021, Waititi said he had finished his Star Wars movie's story, and in 2022, then-Lucasfilm president Kathleen Kennedy said the goal was to bring it to theaters in late 2023. At the time, she also admitted that Disney hadn't "locked anything in" quite yet, a fact that only became more apparent in the years that followed.
points: Director Taika Waititi has confirmed his long-in-development Star Wars movie is officially "on ice.
"I hate to break this to you, but we're going to actually put it on ice and we're working on a different thing together," he said.

articles.title: Silent Hill Remake Studio Wants to Make Physical Games 'for as Long as Possible'
articles.summary: Silent Hill developer Bloober Team wants to make physical versions of its games "for as long as possible." Studio CEO Piotr Babieno opened up about the company's appreciation for physical media and collectibles during an interview with GamesRadar.
body: "Like, OK, the game can have a slightly higher resolution and maybe better lighting and whatever, but will it make it a more engaging game? I don't think so," Babieno said.

The CEO for the studio behind the Silent Hill 2 remake and its in-development original Silent Hill remake also talked about how stats show "the majority of players are playing on hardware which is five, seven years old, if not older." He continued, saying, "But are they less interested in games because of that? I don't think so."

As AI shapes a new, controversial future in the gaming industry, the Bloober executive seems to be more interested in "thinking about other senses." It's this mindset that the team has carried into its new Nintendo Switch 2-exclusive 2.5D horror game, Onyx: The Dark Group. For this experience, which comes from Bloober subsidiary Broken Mirror Games, it's become about "putting horror back in your hands."

"As humans, we have four other senses, and AI can deliver something for what you see, for what you hear, but why not touch?" Babieno said. "I think the physical element of gaming will always, always be there."

articles.title: Adam Scott's Criminally Overlooked 2026 Thriller Is Finally on Streaming
articles.summary: You know it's been a good year for horror movies when a genuine hit still slips through the cracks. We spent the summer on discourse over Obsession, The Backrooms, Zach Cregger's Resident Evil, and The End of Oak Street, all of which pulled in nine-digit takes at the box office.
body: What's interesting about the spread in 2026 is that there's room for every type of horror in the current wave. Only a couple of these movies qualify for the old "elevated horror" (read: the real monster is trauma) designation. The rest are good old-fashioned guts-and-gore flicks.
One 2026 hit that is elevated (occasionally literally) is the Irish ghost story Hokum, which debuted in May to rave reviews and solid ticket sales. It made money but wasn’t a blockbuster.

Looking at the year in horror, Hokum managed to thread a very particular sort of needle; it came out two weeks before Obsession and Backrooms went head-to-head at the box office, so it made its money and got out before the real competition started. If you overlooked Hokum in the middle of all that, it's now streaming on Hulu, and it deserves a place in your cinematic rotation in the run-up to Halloween.

Hokum has such a Stephen King-friendly premise that it's a shock to learn he wasn't involved. Instead, Hokum was written and directed by Damian McCarthy, who previously made 2024's Oddity and 2020's Caveat.
points: You know it's been a good year for horror movies when a genuine hit still slips through the cracks.

articles.title: 63 Years Later, the Stellar Action Comic Strip Most America Never Heard of Deserves Another Shot
articles.summary: This goes double for newspaper comics, which are often viewed as disposable in ways that graphic novels aren't. Surprisingly few of them ever pick up an international audience. Exceptions include Andy Capp and Fred Basset, British strips that have substantially outlived their original creators.
body: One of the cool things about the internet is how it’s become much easier to find obscure comics from all over the world, such as bandes dessinées, science-fiction serials, and stories buried in old magazine anthologies. For every comic that actually gets translated for release outside its original country, such as Valerian or Yoko Tsuno, there are dozens more that don’t. Many of these are long out of print and kept alive online by small communities of fan translators and preservationists. Finding a good one can feel like striking gold.

The British adventure comic Modesty Blaise, created by the late Peter O'Donnell, was virtually unknown in the United States during its original newspaper run, from May 1963 to Feb. 2001. While it has a dedicated audience to this day in much of the rest of the world, over 25 years after it ceased publication, Modesty Blaise was only intermittently carried in American newspapers. This is usually blamed on its frequent nude scenes, which made it too spicy for American audiences. (Modesty is her name, not her practice.) The one exception for years was the Detroit Free Press, and even it censored a couple of strips.

articles.title: 23 devs teamed up to make a free game of 'innovative yet questionable volume sliders,' and it feels like browser-based WarioWare
articles.summary: Volume.art is a nice, free, cool thing on the internet, and I just think that's something worth celebrating these days. The microgame collection sees you manipulating volume sliders through various abstracted, surprising, and very funny ways.
body: It starts strong with "A man named Bow" by Alice Bottino, which kinda reminds me of the Smash Bros Home Run Contest minigame, at least as far as you're winding up to send something from the left side of the screen to the right. You drag back on the mouse to aim a bow and arrow, attempting to land it a set distance (and corresponding volume level) away.

Some of my favorite entries came from Lunacid developer Akuma Kira, like "What's This About," a riff on the criminally-maligned Elder Scrolls Oblivion persuasion pie minigame. You've got to reach a set likability level with a Gamebryo-perfect lumpy potato man, while also accounting for a game-accurate slow decay in persuasiveness as you rapidly cycle between cruelty, honesty, humor, and sucking up.

If I hadn't known about the Oblivion gag going in, it probably would have been my favorite entry⁠—"What's This About" features fairly prominently in volume.art's promo on social media. Surprise and delight is a big part of this thing, and from here there be, uh, spoilers? I guess?

articles.title: New Steam Game is Basically Kiki’s Delivery Service in Video Game Form
articles.summary: Sharing food with others begets a certain type of magic. That goes double for baked goods and desserts. In The Witch’s Bakery, that magic is literal. It’s a charming, cozy, and heartfelt adventure that goes heavy on the Studio Ghibli vibes.
body: In Sunny Lab’s debut game, you play as the heart witch Lunne who moves to Paris and sets up a magical bake shop, along with her pink, cat-like companion Orio. Monday through Saturday, her days are consumed by work. Prepare dough, infuse it with magic, and have Orio bake it with their elemental magic. Tend to customers and rake in that dough. Er, dough being money, in this case.

Some customers are indecisive, while others are impatient. Anyone who’s worked in food service or retail will, unfortunately, not be surprised by the annoyances of those customers. Where Lune’s magic comes into play is for customers haunted by regrets that manifest as cute creatures floating around them, which only the magically inclined can see.

articles.title: Tenebris Somnia Blends 2D Visuals With Live-Action Horror Scenes, And It’s Already On Sale At Launch
articles.summary: Horror games live or die by their scares and tension. If the player isn’t uncomfortable guiding a character through dreadful situations, well, you may as well be playing an action-adventure game (don’t mention the first Uncharted’s final act, please).
body: As the best horror games continue to push for more realistic visuals and immersive experiences, Tenebris Somnia’s twist on the genre combines old-school cool with movie-like cutscenes. It’s both jarring and original, and that’s exactly what makes for excellent horror. I want to be constantly surprised, and Tenebris Somnia makes its pixelated 2D threats even more menacing when you see live-action versions of the monsters.

Co-created by Andrés Borghi and Tobías Rusjan with Saibot Studios, and published by New Blood Interactive, the studio behind Ultrakill, Blood West, and Gloomwood, Tenebris Somnia’s style is fittingly inspired by past eras of console gaming. Its pixelated visuals make the switch to live-action cutscenes even more unsettling. It’s almost like Clock Tower, but if it randomly turned into a movie at any second. No, I’m not shaking; you are.
points: Horror games live or die by their scares and tension.
If the player isn’t uncomfortable guiding a character through dreadful situations, well, you may as well be playing an action-adventure game (don’t mention the first Uncharted’s final act, please).

articles.title: Battlefield 6 devs to fix "Secuty" skin typo, but five-pistol outfit was intentional
articles.summary: Battlefield Studios has responded after fans accused it of using AI to generate cosmetics after spotting a "Secuty" typo on a Battlefield 6 Season 5 skin.
body: The studio acknowledged "candid feedback" from players in a statement on social media, insisting it had "hear[d] your concerns".

And though the statement did not mention AI - either to admit or deny using the generative tech - BattlefieldComm said that while the 'Secuty' typo will be addressed by a "correction update", an outfit with five pistols is intentional.

"First, let's dive into the 'Secuty' typo patches on the McNeil character," the studio wrote. "A correction update has already been planned for the Season 5 Phase 2 release. However, we recognise that letting a known visual error go live without quick acknowledgement creates confusion and erodes trust. We are reviewing how we communicate known visual bugs so you aren’t left wondering whether something was intentional or overlooked."

The five-pistol-touting Midnight Mirage skin, however, is described as an "intentional creative concept" and "a nod to over-the-top action movie tropes where an operative inexplicably has another backup weapon strapped to every spare inch of gear".
points: Battlefield Studios has responded after fans accused it of using AI to generate cosmetics after spotting a "Secuty" typo on a Battlefield 6 Season 5 skin.

articles.title: Dark Souls 2 dataminer shows off massive prototype coliseum level from early development
articles.summary: At a glance. The rough prototype looks to have been binned early in development, and it's largely avoided discussion before Doneda's work. Some portions appear to have been part of an interconnected area, others are likely different versions of the same concept.
body: Doneda, the dataminer who showed off the unused levels, has been proving a genuine authority on Dark Souls 2 in particular. Previously, they made a Nightreign-compatible version of Dark Souls 2's Eleum Loyce. Doneda has also shown off a tantalizingly ambitious early version of Dark Souls 2's The Gutter.

In hindsight, the entire pre-Sekiro Souls series (perhaps sans-Bloodborne) seems defined by difficult, rushed development cycles. Hidetaka Miyazaki took over Demon's Souls partway through as development foundered, and the final game was missing an entire archstone world. Dark Souls has its rougher, less beloved back half, particularly Lost Izalith. Dark Souls 3, though far more consistent than the prior games, had a striking world state system completely struck from it at some point.

body: That article pointed out similarities between these proposals and those used in California's AI legislation, and shares a quote from a spokesperson for the company. "This bill represents the proposals outlined in Anthropic’s Advanced AI Framework, which we have been advocating for with federal and state lawmakers since June," they said, calling "sensible policies we believe Congress should act on."

Just earlier this year, Anthropic's safety lead quit with a note that "the world is in peril" —and just last week, OpenAI was accused by eight US states' attorney generals of ignoring its own safety warnings for the sake of profit. articles.summary: Leaker Kepler_L2 claims the PS6's RAM and NAND alone cost over $680. Sony has said it doesn't intend to sell hardware at significant losses.
body: The PS6's memory and storage reportedly cost more than $680 between them.

That's according to leaker Kepler_L2, who wrote that "RAM + NAND alone is over $680" in a NeoGAF thread in which Kepler_L2 was replying to a forum user who doubted an earlier cost estimate and suggested Sony could subsidise the PS6 to launch at $680.

In June, insider Kepler_L2 - who has previously made claims about hardware that have turned out to be true - claimed the console's bill of materials had climbed to close to $1,000, up from their earlier estimate of around $760.
Kepler_L2 didn't say how they arrived at the figure, and Sony has not, of course, confirmed any PS6 specs or pricing.

articles.title: The Outlast Trials' initial playtests went poorly: Designer says 6-year development took 'a f**king long time' and 'a s**t-ton of prototypes'
articles.summary: Gamedev may as well be conducted in a black box as far as many players are concerned, so it can be easy to think of a good game as one where development went smoothly and a bad game as one where things went terribly awry.
body: As Red Barrels co-founder Philippe Morin told Gamespot in a recent interview, it took six years to turn the vague notion of a co-op Outlast game into something ready to launch via early access. It was "a fucking long time," as he recalled it, and the product of "a shit-ton of prototypes."

"[The Red Barrels team] went too far trying to make [The Outlast Trials] systemic, random, and trying to reach our ultimate goal of infinite replayability," he told Gamespot. "We needed to come back to something that maybe added less replayability, but definitely felt more like Outlast." The article notes that a seemingly shippable build was produced within four years, but playtests went poorly enough to send the team back to the drawing board.

I suppose concerns about replayability have been put to rest now that it's mutated into a sizable live service game with around 20,000 people playing as I write this, though the game's ongoing development isn't entirely free from strife—as the article points out, players are mixed on its use of AI-generated imagery, and Outlast 3 was seemingly put on the backburner after Trials proved a huge success.
